title: How to Plan a Raid (Beginner Guide)
description: The basic plan every raid follows: scout, soak, breach, loot, leave.
requirements: A scout (flyer or Snow Owl for thermal vision)
Explosives for the tier you're breaking
A forward base (FOB) nearby with spare gear in cryopods
steps: Scout: count turrets, Plant Species X, walls and where the vault/dinos probably are.
Build or pick a FOB close by to respawn and resupply.
Soak the turrets until they're empty (see the soaking methods).
Breach with the right explosives for the structure tier.
Grab loot, kill or steal dinos, and leave before the defenders log in.
tips: Raid when the enemy tribe is offline or busy.
Bring more ammo and C4 than you think you need.
Always check the server's structure damage settings.
author: Starter

title: Snow Owl Push (Heal the Soakers)
description: Soakers tank the turrets while Snow Owls heal them fast from out of line of sight, so you can keep pushing without stopping.
requirements: 2+ high-level Snow Owls (level stamina — healing burns stamina and food)
steps: Park the Snow Owls behind cover, out of turret line of sight.
Send the soaker in to drain turrets.
When the soaker is low, pull it back next to the owls.
Use the owl's heal (right-click / freeze ability on the ground) to heal everything around it.
Push the soaker back in. Repeat until the turrets are empty, then breach.
tips: Two owls is ideal on bases with a lot of turrets.
You can start a heal and dismount — the owl keeps healing.
The owl's thermal vision also helps you spot hidden dinos and players.
author: Starter

title: Daeodon Heal Soak
description: The Daeodon heals nearby tames by using up its own food. Cheaper to get than Snow Owls.
requirements: Stacks of meat or kibble to refill it
steps: Put the Daeodon behind cover near the base.
Enable its healing so it heals tames around it.
Rotate hurt soakers back to the Daeodon and swap in fresh ones.
Keep refilling the Daeodon's food.
tips: The Daeodon starves itself while healing — keep an eye on its food bar.
author: Starter

title: Turret Soaking with a Stegosaurus
description: Use a tanky dino to make the turrets waste all their ammo before you go in.
requirements: High-health Stegosaurus (use its plate mode for bullet resistance)
Medical Brews or a healer (Snow Owl / Daeodon)
Optional: more soakers to swap in
steps: Put the Stego in the right plate mode to resist the turret damage type.
Walk just inside turret range so they start firing.
Back out and heal when health gets low, then go back in.
Repeat until the turrets stop firing — they are empty.
Send in the raiding team.
tips: Heavy turrets and Tek turrets hit much harder — bring more soakers.
If turrets target survivors only, you can get shot off your soaker — watch the videos for how to avoid it.
Watch for Plant Species X; it also needs to be soaked or cleared.
author: Starter

title: Gasbag Soaking
description: Gasbags take about 80% less damage while inflated, which makes them one of the best soakers in the game.
requirements: A Quetzal or other flyer to bring them (or cryopods)
steps: Bring the Gasbags near the base in cryopods or with a Quetzal.
Inflate the Gasbag and float it into turret range.
Let the turrets fire at it while it's inflated.
Pull it back to heal, then go again until the turrets are empty.
tips: Great for Aberration and Genesis bases.
Enemies use Snow Owl freeze to deflate Gasbags — watch out for owls.
author: Starter

title: Soaking Tek Turrets
description: Tek turrets use element and hit very hard. Soak them with lots of cheap tames and rotate fast.
requirements: Patience — Tek turrets hold a lot of element
steps: Bring a large number of soakers in cryopods.
Send them in one or a few at a time.
Rotate and heal, or just let the cheap ones die.
Push once the Tek turrets are out of element.
tips: Cheap soakers you don't mind losing are often better than expensive ones here.
author: Starter

title: C4 Breach on a Metal Base
description: The classic raid: blow straight through walls and doors to reach the vault or the tamed dinos.
requirements: Plenty of C4 Charges (always bring more than you think)
A tank dino or teammates to cover you
steps: Scout the base and pick the shortest path to the loot (fewest walls).
Deal with turrets first (soak or destroy them) so you can stand next to the walls.
Stack C4 on one wall or door, step back, and detonate together.
Move one layer at a time and re-check for hidden turrets after every breach.
Grab the loot and get out before the defenders respond.
tips: Doors and gates are often weaker targets than walls.
Check your server's structure damage multiplier before counting C4.
author: Starter

title: Rocket Launcher Turret Clear
description: Take out exposed turrets from outside their range before the main push.
requirements: Spyglass or scope to spot turrets
steps: Walk around the base and mark every turret you can see.
Find a spot outside their range with a clear line of sight.
Fire rockets at one turret at a time until it breaks.
Repeat for the other turrets, then move in.
tips: Turrets behind walls or behind other structures won't be reachable — soak those instead.
Some players combine a Snow Owl freeze with a Tek Gravity Grenade to reach turrets (see the last video).
author: Starter

title: Rocket Turret Siege
description: Build your own Rocket Turret near the enemy base and use it to destroy their defenses.
requirements: A safe spot outside enemy turret range
steps: Build a small protected spot (FOB) near the base.
Place the Rocket Turret and fill it with rockets.
Target turrets and walls from out of their range.
Guard the turret — defenders will try to destroy it.
tips: It's also a strong base defense, so expect the enemy to have them too.
author: Starter

title: Breaking Tek Structures
description: Tek tier is the hardest to break. You need Tek-level damage and a lot of element.
requirements: Tek Grenades / Tek Grenade Launcher / Tek Rifle
steps: Soak or destroy all turrets first, especially Tek Turrets.
Choose the thinnest part of the base.
Use Tek Grenades / Tek damage on the same wall until it breaks.
Push through carefully — Tek bases often have multiple layers.
tips: Farm and craft before the raid; running out of element halfway is the #1 fail.
Tek grenades also work great on ratholes.
author: Starter

title: Tek Mek Siege Cannon
description: The Mek (Extinction / Genesis) can equip a Siege Cannon module that deals huge damage to structures.
steps: Build the Mek and craft the Siege Cannon module.
Get into position where turrets can't easily reach you.
Deploy the siege cannon and fire at walls and turrets.
Push in with the team once there's a hole.
tips: The Mek is big and easy to focus — bring the Mek shield or support.
author: Starter

title: Titanosaur Base Stomp
description: A tamed Titanosaur can smash through structures, but it's hard to keep alive against turrets.
requirements: Support to clear turrets and Plant Species X
Armor for the Titanosaur if available
steps: Soak or clear turrets first — they will chew through the Titanosaur.
Walk the Titanosaur into the base and attack walls.
Keep the team around it to deal with defenders.
tips: Think of it as a one-time weapon — it's very hard to keep alive after a big raid.
author: Starter

title: Underwater Cave Raid (Tek Rifle)
description: Bases hidden in underwater caves (like pearl caves) can be raided with Tek Rifles, which work underwater.
steps: Find the cave entrance and check for underwater turrets.
Soak or shoot turrets with the Tek Rifle.
Break the doors and walls inside.
Take the loot back to the surface.
tips: Underwater Titanosaur-style raids also exist on some caves — see the second video.
author: Starter

title: Tek Rock Drake Cave Raid (Aberration)
description: On Aberration, Rock Drakes can climb walls and ceilings, and with the Tek saddle they can shoot, great for reaching hard cave bases.
steps: Climb to the base from an angle the defenders don't expect (walls/ceiling).
Use the Tek saddle to shoot turrets and structures.
Glide in and breach.
tips: Stay out of the radiation zones or wear a Hazard suit.
author: Starter

title: Clearing Plant Species X
description: Plant Species X is a plant turret that slows and damages you. Clear it before pushing.
requirements: Or a flyer / dino that can hit from outside its range
steps: Find all Plant X around the base.
Stand outside their range and hit them with explosives.
Or soak them like normal turrets, then destroy them.
tips: Plant X is often hidden inside walls or on roofs.
Some defenders make them extra tanky — see the videos for counters.
author: Starter

title: Primitive Siege with Catapult / Cannon
description: Great for primitive servers or early-game bases without heavy defenses.
requirements: Cannon with Cannon Balls (for tougher walls)
A dino or teammate to guard the siege weapon
steps: Place the siege weapon out of the defenders' range.
Aim at one wall and keep firing until it breaks.
Guard the weapon — it's the first thing defenders try to destroy.
Rush in once there's a hole.
tips: Place it behind cover or on high ground so it's harder to hit.
author: Starter

title: Early Game Grenade Raid on Thatch/Wood
description: Cheap and fast way to break weak early-game bases.
steps: Throw grenades at the doors or walls.
Repeat until the structure breaks.
Loot the storage boxes quickly.
tips: Thatch breaks to almost anything; don't waste grenades on it.
author: Starter

title: Offline Raid Timing
description: Not a weapon but a plan: hit the base when the owners are asleep or offline.
requirements: Knowing when the enemy tribe plays
Everything ready in cryopods at a FOB
steps: Watch the tribe for a few days: when do their players log off?
Prepare the whole raid ahead of time.
Start right after they go offline so they can't defend.
Finish fast and leave.
tips: Some servers have offline raid protection (ORP) — check the rules first.
author: Starter
